beats.say: The US Army shows off ENIAC, a computer that weighs thirty tons.
Newspapers call it a giant brain.
beats.head: THE PRESS

beats.say: But six women had programmed it, with no manuals, using cables and switches.
beats.label: SIX PROGRAMMERS

beats.say: Kay McNulty, Jean Jennings, Betty Snyder, Marlyn Wescoff, Fran Bilas and Ruth Lichterman.
beats.head: THE TEAM

beats.say: At the big demonstration, none of them were introduced.
Decades later, a researcher was told they were just models posing with the machine.
Their names stayed almost unknown for half a century.
beats.label: 50 YEARS

beats.say: In 1997, all six entered the Women in Technology Hall of Fame.
Every programmer today works in a job they helped invent.
beats.label: THE FIRST PROGRAMMERS
